decisions.reason: The square-root theorem supplies existence and uniqueness only. Added the direct bound |sqrt(x)-sqrt(y)|²<=|x-y| and continuous-implies-integrable; corrected the separate digest defect to A=2 integral and J_a=A/(2pi). The displayed action and turning-point hypotheses are preserved; all four direct Definition consumers were examined and their mathematical uses remain sound.

The defining power-series citation alone did not justify positivity or measurability. Added differentiability/continuity, endpoint zeros and strict monotonicity to prove sin(theta)>0 on (0,pi), then Borel measurability and the nonnegative-density measure theorem. Branch derivatives already satisfy the nonzero hypothesis of the inverse theorem; AComega is retained.

Given explicitly uses the three ordered tuple entries (u1,u2,u3), so subscripts 1,2,3 name the entries indexed 0,1,2 in the function-space supplier. Relabeling that finite sum gives exactly L2; the cross-product supplier likewise uses named x,y,z entries. Expanding the first component cancels u1v1w1, and cyclic permutation proves the other two. No assertion of a fourth function-space entry occurs.

The Ck supplier is restricted to open sets and was an inaccurate citation for twice differentiable curves on general intervals. Replaced it with iterated domain-relative derivatives from def-derivative, including endpoint limits, preserving the full interval scope. The integral lift uses continuous g with differentiable numerator, and quotient derivatives prove the representation and angle formula at every included endpoint as well.

The open-domain Ck citation did not express the intended interval convention. Defined twice differentiable as iterating def-derivative on I, retaining endpoints and the full claim. Corrected step 1.1 to require only differentiable factors: v-prime need not be twice differentiable. Product rules give w-prime=z-prime=0, constancy supplies A,B, and two differentiations verify the converse.

L3 wrongly quantified x in R^n while summing exactly three standard coordinates; all uses are in R^3. Corrected the dimension and explicitly relabeled the supplier basis. Bessel summed over three standard vectors gives m<=3; the residual orthogonal to a triad must vanish, and the triple identity verifies e1 cross (e3 cross e1)=e3. Statement unchanged.

The cited monotonicity statement alone did not explicitly supply endpoint values. L5 now cites the repaired scattering definition and its complete positivity argument. Compact inverse substitution proves rectangle identities; common finite-measure exhaustion and pi-system uniqueness give the Borel identity, monotone approximation gives nonnegative tests, and positive sine licenses the solid-angle density. Statement unchanged.

Applied the finite-endpoint action theorem on arbitrary bounded positive energy intervals, then used agreement on overlaps and local C1 regularity for all E>0. Period substitution is on interior truncations with positive cosine, followed by independent endpoint limits. Action is E/omega and period is 2pi/omega. Adopted precheck canonical phase numbering: the independent quadrature is step 2.2 and their final comparison is step 3.1; all references preserve the deductions.

The broad inverse differentiability clause of L2 omitted f-prime(c)!=0. Restored this exact hypothesis; V-prime is strictly negative and all actual inverse uses meet it. Energy and the positive potential bound Cartesian speed, compact continuation gives global motion, integrable acceleration gives asymptotic velocities, and the convergent remaining-angle integral gives the impact distance. No conclusion changed.

L4 gave a false global free-speed bound: for mu=J=E=1 and U=-1 near rho=1, rho-prime squared is 3>2, compatible with a smooth finite-range potential and simple outer root rstar=1/2. Restricted the bound to rho>=R where V>=0. Step 2.2 already uses the correct lower bound of V on [rstar,infinity), so continuation, branch uniqueness and quadrature conclusions remain sound without any Statement change.

The phrase asserted inverse names the candidate formula, not a load-bearing inverse axiom. Step 1.1 first proves negative derivative, endpoint limits and bijectivity independently, then defines the cotangent candidate and verifies its composition with theta_def is the identity; injectivity identifies the unique inverse. Its derivative gives the stated density and the theta^-3 bound proves divergence. The pair (theta,b) denotes this forward branch together with its inverse, rather than claiming that an inverse map alone is an impact-to-angle branch.

The rejected prerequisite thm-cm-kepler-conic-and-eccentricity is kind theorem, domain mathematics; its trajectory is an explicitly defined mathematical ODE curve, not a physical postulate or physics theorem. The boundary prohibition therefore does not apply. Completing the square gives the affine disc, polar rays have a unique positive root, and AComega-qualified change of variables and null seam removal prove both area formulas, including e=0.

The conic theorem has no AComega hypothesis; corrected the opening attribution to the ellipse-area and period suppliers while retaining AComega for their actual uses. Direct exact arithmetic gives p=1, a=4/3, b=2sqrt(3)/3, E=-3/8, and both period formulas give T²=256pi²/27. The example remains a conditional algebraic check with no empirical measurement.

downstream_uses.thm-cm-action-variable-derivative:
Statement clause 2 and proof action integral: 1. $a$ and $b$ are of class $C^1$ on $(E_0,E_1)$;
2. the action variable $J_{\mathrm{a}}$ of
   [[def-cm-one-dimensional-action-variable]] is of class $C^1$ on
   $(E_0,E_1)$, and for every $E\in(E_0,E_1)$
   $$J_{\mathrm{a}}'(E)=\frac{1}{2\pi}T(E),\qquad T(E):=\sqrt{2m}\int_{a(E)}^{b(E)}\frac{\mathrm dq}{\sqrt{E-U(q)}}\in(0,\infty),$$
   where the integral is the improper integral over the open interval
   $(a(E),b(E))$, convergent at both endpoints.
downstream_uses.ex-cm-harmonic-oscillator-action-derivat: L1 and Verification steps 1.1, 2.1: [L1] Action variable and theorem: $J_{\mathrm a}(E)=\frac1\pi\int_{a(E)}^{b(E)}\sqrt{2m(E-U(q))}\,\mathrm dq$, and under the two simple turning points of this datum, $J_{\mathrm a}'(E)=T(E)/(2\pi)$ with $T(E)=\sqrt{2m}\int_{a(E)}^{b(E)}\mathrm dq/\sqrt{E-U(q)}$ ([[def-cm-one-dimensional-action-variable]], [[thm-cm-action-variable-derivative]]).
downstream_uses.pthm-cm14-action-angle: Remarks: period-one action is 2pi times the radian action: - **The action coordinates are not unique.** The theorem does not fix additive constants in the actions or constant shifts of the angles: if $(I,\theta)$ has the stated properties then so does $(I+c,\theta)$ for every $c\in\mathbb R^{n}$. In particular the theorem does not by itself single out the classical normalization $I_{i}=\oint_{\gamma_{i}}p\,dq$ of the sources; that normalization is a convention fixed in explicit models, and the one-dimensional companion examples of [[def-cm-one-dimensional-action-variable]] verify it directly in the models treated there, where the period-one action is $2\pi$ times the radian action $J_{\mathrm{a}}$ of that definition.
downstream_uses.ex-cm14-kepler-radial-action-check:
Statement clause 2, L4 and Verification step 3.1: - **Conventions.** $J_{\mathrm a}$ here is the radian action
  $J_{\mathrm a}=\frac1{2\pi}\oint p\,\mathrm dq$ of
  [[def-cm-one-dimensional-action-variable]]; the corresponding
  period-one action of [[pthm-cm14-action-angle]] is its $2\pi$-multiple.
  The identity $J_{\mathrm a}'(E)=T/(2\pi)$ is the one-dimensional
  case of the action-period relation used by the action-angle items of
